column2: Inside a vast white gallery hall whose walls, floor and ceiling are pure white paper covered edge to edge in thick black marker doodles of cartoon animals with speech bubbles, hand drawn and naive, as if a giant drew on the room with a marker, looking straight down the hall to a far wall where a giant marker pen the size of a lamppost leans, a few flower headed visitors far away in black hoodies, soft even gallery light.

Looking straight down a long bank vault corridor with a huge round steel vault door open at the far end, polished black granite floor, walls of brushed steel safe deposit boxes with brass numbers, warm spotlights on six glass display pedestals along the corridor, each pedestal glowing a different colour: holographic rainbow, orange lava, bubblegum pink, white diamond, gold, emerald green, dramatic dark cinematic lighting, nobody near the camera.

A packed trading card tournament hall seen straight down the central aisle: long rows of tables with players with flower heads facing each other over playmats, stacks of booster packs and card boxes, overhead banners that say VEE and NEW YORKERS, a big scoreboard screen at the far end that says FIRST TO SEVEN, foil cards glinting under event lighting, convention centre ceiling, the near tables empty.

A volcanic island at night seen from a black sand beach looking straight at a cartoon shaped but photoreal volcano with glowing orange lava rivers pouring down its sides into the sea, steam, embers floating in the air, a wooden dock running from the camera toward the island, torches along the dock, a crescent moon, dark purple sky, no people near the camera.

Standing at the entrance tunnel of a huge futuristic domed arena looking straight across the sand floor of the arena to the far seats: a glass dome ceiling with purple and gold light, tiers of seats full of flower headed fans, giant screens showing the word VEE, a battle floor marked with a circle, pennants in purple and yellow, dramatic spotlights, nobody near the camera.

Looking straight down a warehouse aisle made entirely of thousands of wrapped gift boxes stacked floor to ceiling in gold, purple and white paper with ribbons, like a wall of presents, three doorways at the far end of decreasing size, warm festive lighting, confetti on the floor far away, nobody near the camera.

Looking straight down the length of an empty indoor basketball court from behind one baseline: polished maple floor with painted lines, the far hoop and backboard, bleachers on both sides with a few flower headed fans, banners in purple and yellow that say VEE and NEW YORKERS, bright gym lights, the near court completely empty.

Inside a huge old newspaper printing hall looking straight down the length of a roaring printing press line: giant rolls of newsprint, the long press machines, pages flying along overhead on a rail, stacks of Sunday comics sections in colour on pallets, ink smell, industrial windows with morning light, workers with flower heads far away, nobody near the camera.

Looking straight down a toy store aisle at Christmas: tall shelves on both sides packed with boxed vinyl figures of cartoon animals with blank boxes in purple and yellow, plush animals piled high, a claw machine at the far end glowing, a checkout with a flower headed cashier far away, warm store lighting, polished floor, nobody near the camera.

Looking straight down a dark gallery of pixel art: both walls are a grid of hundreds of small square portraits in 24 by 24 pixels, each a different pixel character with a flower for a head, lit by thin LED strips, at the far end three giant pixel figures made of glowing cubes stand like statues, black floor reflecting the light, a velvet rope far away, nobody near the camera.

Looking straight down the main floor of a vast wine store with a mezzanine balcony running all the way round: tens of thousands of wine bottles in wooden racks from floor to ceiling, a tasting counter at the far end with a silver bucket, warm pendant lights, hand written shelf tags that say NEW YORKERS and MLOW, a staircase up to the mezzanine on the right, polished concrete floor, a few flower headed shoppers far away.

Standing on the goal line of a football field at night looking straight down the field: green grass with white yard lines and numbers, the far goal posts, a packed stadium in green and white under floodlights, breath steam, a scoreboard reading 5 to 5, confetti, the field empty near the camera.

Looking straight down a long dark corridor whose walls, floor and ceiling are made of hundreds of vertical phone screens, each playing a different short video of city life with flower headed people, caption text on the screens in bold white letters that say NEW YORKERS, VEE, CLOUDS AND DIRT, the corridor glowing in cyan and pink from the screens, at the far end a giant glowing thumb icon, nobody near the camera.
